pr_body:
This PR adds a check that relies on 7.17 calculating the overall index age
metadata from the existing indices we have. Once we have the oldest index
age computed, we add a check to prevent upgrades to 8.0 with any indices
that are older than 7.0.

Closes  #81326
pr_title: Prevent direct upgrade of indices from 6.8 to 8.0
pr_comment: Hi @grcevski, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
Still a draft because I need to figure out how to test this, other than the manual testing I did.
Disabling bwc tests until the change is backported to 7.17 and 8.0. Otherwise all upgrade tests fail because we expect to see metadata there.

7.17 PR backport can be found here https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/82771. The backport can't be direct because the 7 source is sufficiently different, and the actual 7.17 logic is not the same because we don't do the compatibility check there, we only compute the oldest index version.

## 💔 Backport failed
| Status | Branch | Result |
|:------:|:------:|:------:|
| ❌ |  8.0  | Commit could not be cherrypicked due to conflicts |

You can use [sqren/backport](https://github.com/sqren/backport) to manually backport by running `backport --upstream elastic/elasticsearch --pr 82689`

review_comment: We assert when loading the data that the commit's `userData` has this many entries, which will fail in upgrades from a 4-entry to a 5-entry commit I think.
Should we set `oldestIndexVersion` back to `Version.V_EMPTY` here if the key is missing? Otherwise we end up returning a `NodeMetadata` that never really existed. Super-rare case I know...
Good catch, it's safest to do it!

This is only used in the legacy format which we shouldn't really be reading here, but I think this means that the index compatibility check will fail before the node version check happens, so the error will say that there are some ancient indices rather than that the previous node version is too old. I wonder if it would be better to check the index version in `NodeMetadata#upgradeToCurrentVersion` and just call that in both places so we have consistent checks.

Yes exactly. I was testing direct to 8 upgrade from 6.8 and this showed up. Right now it says you have indices from version 0.0.0, which does the job but isn't the best. Good suggestion, I'll extract the upgrade/downgrade check on the metadata in a separate method and call that ahead.
